text:
Maria Gomez: Heads-up — while onboarding mosaic-7b-v1 (HF) to Redwood I found a weird special-token ID drift after the conversion. BOS and EOS IDs look swapped and a few added_tokens ended up with shifted IDs. Repro steps below.
Raj Patel: Oof, can you paste the tokenizer header and added_tokens? small snippet pls :thinking:
Maria Gomez: Sure. From HF tokenizer.json before conversion:
```json
{
  "bos_token_id": 1,
  "eos_token_id": 2,
  "unk_token_id": 0,
  "pad_token_id": 3,
  "added_tokens": ["<URL>", "<CODE_SNIPPET>"]
}
```
After running our hf-to-redwood tool I see:
```json
{
  "bos_token_id": 2,
  "eos_token_id": 1,
  "unk_token_id": 0,
  "pad_token_id": 3,
  "added_tokens": ["<URL>", "<CODE_SNIPPET>"]
}
```
IDs for the byte-level vocab were also renumbered — `added_tokens` themselves appear in-place but the global token IDs shifted by +1 for a block, causing mismatch with KV cache indices.
Liam Chen: Did you run quantize/merge steps? Sometimes our encoder merges (merge_vocab + fasttokenizer rebuild) reindex base tokens and then appended added_tokens get remapped incorrectly.
Maria Gomez: Yes: pipeline was `hf->merge-vocab->tokenizer-rebuild->quantize`. Problem shows before quantize (after rebuild). Command I ran:
```
./tools/hf_to_redwood --input hf-tokenizer.json --vocab vocab.json --out redwood-tokenizer.json
```
Sasha Ivanova: Can you share the exact diff that shows mapping drift? small `grep` output is enough.
Maria Gomez: grep of token ids around BOS/EOS:
```
$ jq '.tokens[0:6]' vocab.json
["<unk>", "<bos>", "<eos>", "<pad>", " the", " of"]
$ jq '.tokens[0:6]' redwood_vocab.json
["<unk>", "<eos>", "<bos>", "<pad>", " the", " of"]
```
So the order of the two specials got flipped during the token merge step.
Raj Patel: That explains some chat regressions — template code assumes bos==1 and eos==2 at runtime. If those are swapped then prefix caching and stopping criteria break. Quick mitigation: add a tokenizer alias map at runtime that remaps indices back to HF expectation.
Maria Gomez: Yup tried a quick runtime shim: remap_table = {1:2, 2:1} for special tokens and it restored chat stopping but broke embedding alignment (embedding matrix index != token id). Not safe long term.
Liam Chen: Root cause hypothesis: our merge script sorts specials by token string (lexicographic) before assigning reserved IDs. If HF tokenizer had a different internal ordering, the conversion tool's stable sort flipped the two. Also added_tokens insertion index was computed relative to pre-merged index, so block shift happened.
Sasha Ivanova: Can we reproduce in a minimal script? If so we should add a unit test to conversion that asserts preserved special-token semantics (`bos_token_id`, `eos_token_id`, `pad_token_id`, `unk_token_id`) and that `added_tokens` map to stable IDs.
Maria Gomez: I created a small repro in `eng-ml/convert_tests/test_special_token_preserve.py` locally. Steps: export HF tokenizer json, run conversion, assert ids identical. Fails.
deploy-bot: conversion-tool v2.3 ran by Maria Gomez on branch `mosaic-import-fix` — job 4821 queued.
Raj Patel: Proposed fix: change merge-vocab to reserve first N special slots (explicit mapping) instead of sorting. Also, when inserting `added_tokens`, compute their final ID after merges and write an explicit `token_id_map` into `redwood-tokenizer.json` (like `{ "<URL>": 50256 }`). Then runtime can validate and fail fast if mismatch.
Liam Chen: Additional check: when we quantize weights we must not assume token id order. Embed matrix needs to be reindexed to the final token ID ordering. Add a reindex step: `reindex_embeddings(vocab_map, embed.npy)`.
Maria Gomez: I pushed a patch that does the reserved-slot approach and added a failing unit test. Patch: `tools/hf_to_redwood: reserve_specials=True` default now. CI shows one more failure for a model with a custom PAD id (non-standard). Will handle edge-case.
Sasha Ivanova: Nice. Can you also add an eval that runs a small prompt set checking: stop tokens, chat-format boundaries and embeddings-bucket-sanity? We should detect quality regressions automatically.
Maria Gomez: Yep adding eval harness into `onboarding/evals/special-token-regression` — will run on nightly for all new model imports.
Raj Patel: Short-term mitigation for prod — add a conversion-time validation that compares HF tokenizer `special_tokens_map` to the result and aborts with human-readable diff if mismatch. Don't let bad imports hit dedicated/private without signoff.
Maria Gomez: Agreed. I'll open a PR for the validation + reindex embed step and tag you all. Thanks for the quick triage :raised_hands:
Liam Chen: Nice work catching this before rollout. :thumbsup:
Sasha Ivanova: Good call. Once PR lands, let's run full regression on the mosaic-7b family and flag any quantization combos that re-trigger reindexing bugs.
Maria Gomez: Will do, pushing tests + docs. If anyone wants to pair on the embed reindexer ping me.
Raj Patel: FYI I'll add a quick Canary rule in Redwood Console to detect token-id mismatch errors (runtime logs) and route traffic to fallback model variant.
Maria Gomez: Perfect. I'll follow up with the PR link and a short postmortem note in the onboarding checklist when fixed.
